newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends slightly firmer on dollar sales.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends slightly firmer on dollar sales.

text.p: The won closed slightly firmer against the dollar on Monday as dollar unwinding, prompted by expectations of dollar supplies in early July, outweighed short-cover dollar buying, dealers said.
"Actual dollar positions look shallow. But expectations of dollar inflows pushed some banks to go short in dollars," said a domestic bank dealer.
The won closed at 887.90 against Friday's close of 888.10. It opened at 888.00 and moved between 887.50 and 888.30.
Dealers said the central bank may intervene to support the dollar on Tuesday if the won rose to 887.20/50.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 887.90 on Tuesday, compared with 888.10 today.
Dealers forecast trading would range from 887.50 to 888.30/50 on Tuesday.
